title: Adaptive per-shard quant defaults and calibration sampling strategy
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Many models have heterogeneous activation distributions across attention heads and per-layer sharding. A single per-model 'default' quant profile (e.g., FP8 static or INT8 symmetric) sometimes underestimates worst-case accuracy degradation on long-tail inputs or high-temperature sampling. Current catalog entries expose a handful of presets, but lack: (1) per-shard (per-slice) safe thresholds, (2) an automated sampling strategy for calibration datasets that surfaces fragile model regions, and (3) runtime guardrails for dynamic fallback when drift is detected.

Goal:
Define and implement a system for generating per-model quantization defaults that include: recommended FP8/INT8 profiles, per-shard tolerance thresholds, a reproducible calibration sampling pipeline, and runtime guardrails that can gracefully fall back to a safer profile when production data indicates quality regressions. Deliverables: catalog metadata schema additions, calibration harness updates, CI gating rules, runtime telemetry signals, and a rollout plan for existing catalog entries.

Scope (what's included):
- Extend model-catalog metadata to include: primary_profile, safe_profile_chain, per_shard_tolerance (numeric band), calibration_seed_hash, and validation_examples_summary (small fingerprint).
- Implement a calibration sampler that: stratifies by sequence length / position, temperature / decoding mode (greedy / top-k / top-p), and diversified prompt templates derived from the model's eval set and production prefix fingerprints.
- Produce automated validation metrics: EM/ROUGE/embedding-similarity deltas, token-level perplexity increase, and hallucination score heuristics on critical prompt slices.
- Create runtime guardrail heuristics: if median embedding-similarity to calibration baseline drops by > X% on 1% of requests, trigger a canary fallback to safe_profile_chain, and emit alerts.
- Add CI gates: quant profiles must pass shadow-eval on top-N prompts with no more than 0.5% regression in primary accuracy metric or be flagged for manual review.

Out of scope:
- Full model re-training for quantization-aware training (QAT) — we will rely on post-training calibration and tuning only.
- Integration with Dedicated autoscaler policies (tracked separately).

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Catalog metadata schema is extended and backward compatible.
- For 3 target models (small/mid/large), calibration pipeline produces a recommended primary profile and safe_profile_chain with per_shard_tolerance numbers.
- Shadow-eval CI for quant profiles is implemented and passing for the 3 target models in the validation matrix.
- Runtime telemetry emits the defined signals and a test harness simulates a drift event that triggers a fallback to safe profile.
- Documentation (console + API) updated with examples and rollout checklist.

Design decisions and tradeoffs considered:
- Per-shard tolerances are more precise but increase metadata surface area; we will default to coarse-grained tolerances for small models and enable fine-grained shards for larger models where telemetry shows variance.
- FP8 is preferred for throughput on supported hardware; INT8 is required as a deterministic fallback on non-FP8 runtime paths. Catalog entries will recommend FP8 primary where validation shows <0.5% quality delta, otherwise pick INT8.
- Sampling must balance cost vs coverage: initial sampler will use a 10k-example budget per model with stratified buckets; we may lower for tiny models.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Calibration harness: add new job type quant-calibrate-v2 in infra pipelines with inputs: model-artifact, eval-set-sources (S3/GDrive), sampling-seed, decoding-modes. Outputs: profile.json, per_shard_tolerance.csv, validation_manifest.json, fingerprint hash.
- Catalog metadata keys (strings): primary_profile, safe_profile_chain (comma-separated), per_shard_tolerance (comma-separated floats), calibration_seed_hash, validation_examples_summary.
- Shadow-eval results are stored in the eval-db; gating will query eval-db by calibration_seed_hash.
- Runtime enforcement: lightweight checks in serving layer that compute embedding similarity against stored calibration centroids (first 64 tokens) using an L2 threshold; implement in runtime-telemetry module to avoid adding latency to critical path (async check + logging).

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New metrics: quant.profile_applied, quant.embedding_similarity.delta, quant.fallback_triggered, quant.shadow_eval_regress_pct.
- Console dashboard: per-model quant-health panel and recent fallback events with link to example requests.

Validation plan and benchmarks:
- Target models: small-chat-1, conv-midsize-3, longform-8b.
- For each model run: baseline FP16 eval, candidate FP8/INT8 evals across decoding modes + top 5 high-sensitivity prompts. Record token throughput / latency and accuracy delta.
- Benchmarks: aim for <10% median latency regression and <0.5% accuracy regression for primary_profile compared to FP16 baseline. Safe_profile_chain must guarantee <0.1% degradation compared to baseline.

Rollout plan:
1) Schema and calibration harness merged behind feature flag. 2) Generate profiles for internal models and run shadow-eval CI. 3) Add telemetry and greylist fallback in sandbox environment. 4) Canary: enable profile metadata for 10% of hosted traffic with automatic rollback. 5) Full roll when no regressions seen for 2 weeks.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Adaptive+Quant+Defaults+Design
- Calibration harness prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5231
- Eval notebooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_sample_folder
- Shadow-eval dashboard (internal): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/quant-shadow
